specAnchors.text: know that alcohols contain the functional group −OH

understand how to draw structural and displayed formulae for methanol, ethanol, propanol (propan-1-ol only) and butanol (butan-1-ol only), and name each compound the names propanol and butanol are acceptable

primer.text: From Bromine & Alkenes you already know how a functional group dictates a reaction test. This note closes the wave on a third functional group: the hydroxyl group of the alcohols, the family behind fuels and spirits, with the naming twist that trades a final e for an ol.

modules.title: The hydroxyl group that defines the family
modules.opening: Alcohols are colourless liquids that mix with water and burn as fuels. This lesson fixes the one feature that makes them a family: the hydroxyl group responsible for their characteristic reactions.
keyPoints: Alcohols are clear liquids that mix with water, giving neutral solutions.
The first four members of the family serve as common fuels.
Every alcohol carries the hydroxyl group, written -OH.
The hydroxyl group is the part of the molecule responsible for the characteristic reactions of alcohols.
In ethanol the -OH side chain is what characterises its chemistry, as the diagram of the molecule shows.

low.restatement: Alcohols are clear liquids that mix with water into neutral solutions and burn well as fuels. What makes them a family is the -OH hydroxyl group every member carries. Fuels and spirits alike belong to this one family.
low.analogy: The -OH group is a family badge worn by every alcohol; the carbon chain behind it may vary, but the badge decides how the whole family behaves.
low.examPointer: Write the functional group as -OH, and quote neutral solutions when describing their behaviour in water.

medium.restatement: Alcohols are colourless liquids dissolving in water to give neutral solutions, and the first four members serve as common fuels. Their shared feature is the hydroxyl functional group, -OH, the bonded arrangement that governs the characteristic reactions distinguishing alcohols from alkanes and alkenes.
medium.analogy: If the carbon chain is the furniture of the molecule, the -OH group is the mains socket: whatever the furniture, that socket decides which appliances, meaning reactions, can be plugged in.
medium.examPointer: Name the group and its consequence together: -OH present, therefore the characteristic alcohol reactions follow.

modules.title: The first four alcohols
modules.opening: Naming alcohols reuses the alkane system with one letter swap. This lesson lines up methanol to butan-1-ol with their formulae and decodes what the number in the name records.
keyPoints: The first four alcohols are methanol CH3OH, ethanol C2H5OH, propan-1-ol C3H7OH and butan-1-ol C4H9OH.
Naming uses the alkane and alkene system with the final e replaced by ol.
Propanol and butanol are acceptable names for propan-1-ol and butan-1-ol in exams.
The 1 in propan-1-ol records that the -OH group sits on the first carbon atom.
Structural and displayed formulae show the OH group hanging on the carbon chain of each member.

low.restatement: Take the alkane name, drop the final e and add ol: methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol, butan-1-ol. The number says which carbon carries the OH, and short names propanol and butanol are accepted.
low.analogy: It is the alkane surname with a new ending swapped in, like a marriage certificate: same family line, new chemical identity announced by the ol.
low.examPointer: Either form, propan-1-ol or propanol, earns the mark, but draw the OH on the first carbon when the 1 is quoted.

medium.restatement: The homologous run runs methanol CH3OH, ethanol C2H5OH, propan-1-ol C3H7OH and butan-1-ol C4H9OH, named by replacing the alkane final e with ol. The position number fixes which carbon bears the OH group, the first carbon for the butan-1-ol of this course, and the shortened names propanol and butanol are acceptable.
medium.analogy: Think of the carbon chain as a numbered terrace of houses: the stem names the street, the suffix ol says a hydroxyl resident lives there, and the number gives the house where it moved in.
medium.examPointer: Draw the displayed formula with OH on the stated carbon, and remember the spec accepts propanol and butanol as names.

glossary.definition: A member of the homologous series carrying the hydroxyl group, neutral in water and usable as fuels.
The -OH arrangement of atoms bonded to the carbon chain, responsible for the characteristic reactions of alcohols.
The one-carbon alcohol, CH3OH, the first member of the series.
The two-carbon alcohol, C2H5OH, whose molecule shows the OH side chain clearly.
The three-carbon alcohol, C3H7OH, with the OH group on the first carbon; propanol is acceptable.
